sourceChapterWithLineNumbers:
1:   Krishna.
2:   Men call the Aswattha,--the Banyan-tree,--
3:   Which hath its boughs beneath, its roots above,--
4:   The ever-holy tree. Yea! for its leaves
5:   Are green and waving hymns which whisper Truth!
6:   Who knows the Aswattha, knows Veds, and all.
7: 
8:   Its branches shoot to heaven and sink to earth,[FN#30]
9:   Even as the deeds of men, which take their birth
10:     From qualities: its silver sprays and blooms,
11:   And all the eager verdure of its girth,
12:   Leap to quick life at kiss of sun and air,
13:   As men's lives quicken to the temptings fair
14:     Of wooing sense: its hanging rootlets seek
15:   The soil beneath, helping to hold it there,
16: 
17:   As actions wrought amid this world of men
18:   Bind them by ever-tightening bonds again.
19:     If ye knew well the teaching of the Tree,
20:   What its shape saith; and whence it springs; and, then
21: 
22:   How it must end, and all the ills of it,
23:   The axe of sharp Detachment ye would whet,
24:     And cleave the clinging snaky roots, and lay
25:   This Aswattha of sense-life low,--to set
26: 
27:   New growths upspringing to that happier sky,--
28:   Which they who reach shall have no day to die,
29:     Nor fade away, nor fall--to Him, I mean,
30:   FATHER and FIRST, Who made the mystery
31: 
32:   Of old Creation; for to Him come they
33:   From passion and from dreams who break away;
34:     Who part the bonds constraining them to flesh,
35:   And,--Him, the Highest, worshipping alway--
36: 
37:   No longer grow at mercy of what breeze
38:   Of summer pleasure stirs the sleeping trees,
39:     What blast of tempest tears them, bough and stem
40:   To the eternal world pass such as these!
41: 
42:   Another Sun gleams there! another Moon!
43:   Another Light,--not Dusk, nor Dawn, nor Noon--
44:     Which they who once behold return no more;
45:   They have attained My rest, life's Utmost boon!
46: 
47:   When, in this world of manifested life,
48:   The undying Spirit, setting forth from Me,
49:   Taketh on form, it draweth to itself
50:   From Being's storehouse,--which containeth all,--
51:   Senses and intellect. The Sovereign Soul
52:   Thus entering the flesh, or quitting it,
53:   Gathers these up, as the wind gathers scents,
54:   Blowing above the flower-beds. Ear and Eye,
55:   And Touch and Taste, and Smelling, these it takes,--
56:   Yea, and a sentient mind;--linking itself
57:   To sense-things so.
58: 
59:   The unenlightened ones
60:   Mark not that Spirit when he goes or comes,
61:   Nor when he takes his pleasure in the form,
62:   Conjoined with qualities; but those see plain
63:   Who have the eyes to see. Holy souls see
64:   Which strive thereto. Enlightened, they perceive
65:   That Spirit in themselves; but foolish ones,
66:   Even though they strive, discern not, having hearts
67:   Unkindled, ill-informed!
68: 
69:   Know, too, from Me
70:   Shineth the gathered glory of the suns
71:   Which lighten all the world: from Me the moons
72:   Draw silvery beams, and fire fierce loveliness.
73:   I penetrate the clay, and lend all shapes
74:   Their living force; I glide into the plant--
75:   Root, leaf, and bloom--to make the woodlands green
76:   With springing sap. Becoming vital warmth,
77:   I glow in glad, respiring frames, and pass,
78:   With outward and with inward breath, to feed
79:   The body by all meats.[FN#31]
80: 
81:   For in this world
82:   Being is twofold: the Divided, one;
83:   The Undivided, one. All things that live
84:   Are "the Divided." That which sits apart,
85:   "The Undivided."
86: 
87:   Higher still is He,
88:   The Highest, holding all, whose Name is LORD,
89:   The Eternal, Sovereign, First! Who fills all worlds,
90:   Sustaining them. And--dwelling thus beyond
91:   Divided Being and Undivided--I
92:   Am called of men and Vedas, Life Supreme,
93:   The PURUSHOTTAMA.
94: 
95:   Who knows Me thus,
96:   With mind unclouded, knoweth all, dear Prince!
97:   And with his whole soul ever worshippeth Me.
98: 
99: 
100:   Now is the sacred, secret Mystery
101:   Declared to thee! Who comprehendeth this
102:   Hath wisdom! He is quit of works in bliss!
103: 
104:   HERE ENDS CHAPTER XV. OF THE BHAGAVAD-GITA
105:   Entitled "Purushottamapraptiyog,"
106:   Or "The Book of Religion by attaining the Supreme."

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 15.1 The Blessed Lord said They (the wise) speak of the indestructible peepul tree having its root above and branches below, whose leaves are the metres or hymns: he who knows it is a knower of the Vedas.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 15.1 "Lord Shri Krishna continued: This phenomenal creation, which is both ephemeral and eternal, is like a tree, but having its seed above in the Highest and its ramifications on this earth below. The scriptures are its leaves, and he who understands this, knows.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 15.1 The Blessed Lord said They say that the peepul Tree, which has its roots upward and the branches downward, and of which the Vedas are the leaves, is imperishable. He who realizes it is knower of the Vedas.

arnold.content:
Its branches shoot to heaven and sink to earth,[FN#30]
  Even as the deeds of men, which take their birth
    From qualities: its silver sprays and blooms,
  And all the eager verdure of its girth,
  Leap to quick life at kiss of sun and air,
  As men's lives quicken to the temptings fair
    Of wooing sense: its hanging rootlets seek
  The soil beneath, helping to hold it there,

  As actions wrought amid this world of men
  Bind them by ever-tightening bonds again.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 15.2 Below and above spread its branches, nourished by the Gunas; sense-objects are its buds; and below, in the world of men, stretch forth the roots, originating action.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 15.2 Its branches shoot upwards and downwards, deriving their nourishment from the Qualities; its buds are the objects of sense; and its roots, which follow the Law causing man's regeneration and degeneration, pierce downwards into the soil.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 15.2 The branches of that (Tree), extending down-wards and upwards, are strengthened by the alities and have sense-objects as their shoots. And the roots, which are followed by actions, spread down-wards in the human world [According to A.G. and M.S. manusya-loke means a body distinguished by Brahminhood etc.].

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 15.4 Then That goal should be sought for, whither having gone none returns again. I seek refuge in that Primeval Purusha Whence streamed forth the ancient activity or energy.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 15.4 Beyond lies the Path, from which, when found, there is no return. This is the Primal God from whence this ancient creation has sprung.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 15.4 Thereafter, that State has to be sought for, going where they do not return again: I take refuge in that Primeval Person Himself, from whom has ensued the eternal Manifestation.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 15.5 Free from pride and delusion, victorious over the evil of attachment, dwelling constantly in the Self, their desires having completely turned away, freed from the pairs of opposites known as pleasure and pain, the undeluded reach the eternal goal.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 15.5 The wise attain Eternity when, freed from pride and delusion, they have conquered their love for the things of sense; when, renouncing desire and fixing their gaze on the Self, they have ceased to be tossed to and fro by the opposing sensations, like pleasure and pain.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 15.5 The wise ones who are free from pride and non-discrimination, who have conered the evil of association, [Hatred and love arising from association with foes and friends.] who are ever devoted to spirituality, completely free from desires, free from the dualities called happiness and sorrow, reach that undecaying State.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 15.6 Neither the sun nor the moon nor fire illumines That. That is My supreme Abode, reaching which they do not return.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 15.7 An eternal portion of Myself having become a living soul in the world of life, draws to (itself) the (five) senses with the mind for the sixth, abiding in Nature.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 15.7 It is only a very small part of My Eternal Self, which is the life of the universe, drawing round itself the six senses, the mind the last, which have their source in Nature.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 15.7 It is verily a part of Mine which, becoming the eternal individual soul in the region of living beings, draws (to itself) the organs which have the mind as their sixth, and which abide in Nature.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 15.8 When the Lord (as the individual soul) obtains a body and when He leaves it, He takes these and goes (with them) as the wind takes the scents from their seats (flowers, etc.).

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 15.8 When the Supreme Lord enters a body or leaves it, He gathers these senses together and travels on with them, as the wind gathers perfume while passing through the flowers.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 15.8 When the master leaves it and even when he assumes a body, he departs taking these, as wind (carries away) odours from their receptacles.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 15.12 That light in the sun which illumines the whole world, that which is in the moon, and that which is in fire,-know that light to be Mine.

witnesses.text: 15.13 And entering the earth I sustain the beings through (My) power; and nourish all the plants by becoming Soma [According to S. and most other translators, Soma means the moon.-Tr.] which is of the nature of sap.

records.sanskrit:
अहं वैश्वानरो भूत्वा प्राणिनां देहमाश्रितः।
प्राणापानसमायुक्तः पचाम्यन्नं चतुर्विधम् ॥
records.iast:
ahaṃ vaiśvānaro bhūtvā prāṇināṃ dehamāśritaḥ
prāṇāpānasamāyuktaḥ pacāmyannaṃ caturvidham
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Becoming vital warmth,
  I glow in glad, respiring frames, and pass,
  With outward and with inward breath, to feed
  The body by all meats.[FN#31]

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 15.14 Having become the fire Vaisvanara, I abide in the body of living beings and, associated with the Prana and the Apana, digest the fourfold food.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 15.14 Becoming the fire of life, I pass into their bodies and, uniting with the vital streams of Prana and Apana, I digest the various kinds of food.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 15.14 Taking the form of Vaisvanara and residing in the bodies of creatures, I, in association with Prana and Apana, digest the four kinds of food.

records.sanskrit:
सर्वस्य चाहं हृदि सन्निविष्टो
मत्तः स्मृतिर्ज्ञानमपोहनञ्च।
वेदैश्च सर्वैरहमेव वेद्यो
वेदान्तकृद्वेदविदेव चाहम् ॥
records.iast:
sarvasya cāhaṃ hṛdi sanniviṣṭo mattaḥ smṛtirjñānamapohanañca
vedaiśca sarvairahameva vedyo vedāntakṛdvedavideva cāham
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.note: Arnold omits the verse about memory, knowledge, and the Vedas; translator note 31 explicitly says he omits a verse at this point.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 15.15 And I am seated in the hearts of all; from Me are memory and knowledge, as well as their absence. I am verily That which has to be known by all the Vedas; I am indeed the author of the Vedanta and the knower of the Vedas am I.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 15.15 I am enthroned in the hearts of all; memory, wisdom and discrimination owe their origins to Me. I am He Who is to be realised in the scriptures; I inspire their wisdom and I know their truth.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 15.15 And I am seated in the hearts of all. From Me are memory, knowledge and their loss. I alone am the object to be known through all the Vedas; I am also the originator of the Vedanta, and I Myself am the knower of the Vedas.

records.sanskrit:
द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके क्षरश्चाक्षर एव च।
क्षरः सर्वाणि भूतानि कूटस्थोऽक्षर उच्यते ॥
records.iast:
dvāvimau puruṣau loke kṣaraścākṣara eva ca
kṣaraḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni kūṭastho.akṣara ucyate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
For in this world
  Being is twofold: the Divided, one;
  The Undivided, one. All things that live
  Are "the Divided." That which sits apart,
  "The Undivided."

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
15.16 Two Purushas there are in this world, the perishable and the imperishable. All beings are
the perishable and the Kutastha the unchanging is called the imperishable.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 15.16 There are two aspects in Nature: the perishable and the imperishable. All life in this world belongs to the former, the unchanging element belongs to the latter.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 15.16 There are these two persons in the world-the mutable and the immutable. The mutable consists of all things; the one existing as Maya is called the immutable.

records.sanskrit:
उत्तमः पुरुषस्त्वन्यः परमात्मेत्युधाहृतः।
यो लोकत्रयमाविश्य बिभर्त्यव्यय ईश्वरः ॥
records.iast:
uttamaḥ puruṣastvanyaḥ paramātmetyudhāhṛtaḥ
yo lokatrayamāviśya bibhartyavyaya īśvaraḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Higher still is He,
  The Highest, holding all, whose Name is LORD,
  The Eternal, Sovereign, First! Who fills all worlds,
  Sustaining them.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 15.17 But distinct is the Supreme Purusha called the highest Self, the indestructible Lord Who, pervading the three worlds, sustains them.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 15.17 But higher than all am I, the Supreme God, the Absolute Self, the Eternal Lord, Who pervades the worlds and upholds them all.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 15.17 But different is th supreme Person who is spoken of as the transcendental Self, who, permeating the three worlds, upholds (them), and is the imperisahble God.

records.sanskrit:
यस्मात्क्षरमतीतोऽहमक्षरादपि चोत्तमः।
अतोऽस्मि लोके वेदे च प्रथितः पुरुषोत्तमः ॥
records.iast:
yasmātkṣaramatīto.ahamakṣarādapi cottamaḥ
ato.asmi loke vedeca prathitaḥ puruṣottamaḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
And--dwelling thus beyond
  Divided Being and Undivided--I
  Am called of men and Vedas, Life Supreme,
  The PURUSHOTTAMA.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 15.18 As I transcend the perishable and am even higher than the imperishable, I am declared to be the highest Purusha in the world and in the Vedas.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 15.18 Beyond comparison of the Eternal with the non-eternal am I, Who am called by scriptures and sages the Supreme Personality, the Highest God.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 15.18 Since I am transcendental to the mutable and above even the immutable, hence I am well known in the world and in the Vedas as the supreme Person.

records.sanskrit:
यो मामेवमसम्मूढो जानाति पुरुषोत्तमम्।
स सर्वविद्भजति मां सर्वभावेन भारत ॥
records.iast:
yo māmevamasammūḍho jānāti puruṣottamam
sa sarvavidbhajati māṃ sarvabhāvena bhārata
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Who knows Me thus,
  With mind unclouded, knoweth all, dear Prince!
  And with his whole soul ever worshippeth Me.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 15.19 He who, undeluded, knows Me thus as the highest Purusha, he, knowing all, worships Me with his whole being (heart), O Arjuna.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 15.19 He who with unclouded vision sees Me as the Lord-God, knows all there is to be known, and always shall worship Me with his whole heart.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 15.19 O scion of the Bharata dynasty, he who, being free from delusion, knows Me the supreme Person thus, he is all-knowing and adores Me with his whole being.

records.sanskrit:
इति गुह्यतमं शास्त्रमिदमुक्तं मयानघ।
एतद्बुद्ध्वा बुद्धिमान्स्यात्कृतकृत्यश्च भारत ॥
records.iast:
iti guhyatamaṃ śāstramidamuktaṃ mayānagha
etadbuddhvā buddhimānsyātkṛtakṛtyaśca bhārata
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Now is the sacred, secret Mystery
  Declared to thee! Who comprehendeth this
  Hath wisdom! He is quit of works in bliss!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 15.20 Thus, this most secret science has been taught by Me, O sinless one; on knowing this, a man becomes wise, and all his duties are accomplished, O Arjuna.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 15.20 Thus, O Sinless One, I have revealed to thee this most mystic knowledge. He who understands gains wisdom and attains the consummation of life."

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 15.20 O sinless one, this most secret scripture has thus been uttered by Me. Understanding this, one becomes wise and has his duties fulfilled, O scion of the Bharata dynasty.
